applies_why: The judge text evaluates a link against the challenger's pressed covenant-origin chain and then uses the single sentence's own wording as the deciding point.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: "never verse by verse" and the retired stating-verse test: I weighed whether the judge resolved the collision by chain-against-chain footing or instead by one sentence's own words; the latter reading makes it a verse-level stating test.
why: The judge recognized the challenger's chain as footed but then decided the link by the sentence's own words, which is the verse-level stating-verse approach K-C retires rather than a chain-against-chain footing comparison.
